ns1:item.ns1:title: MALS-Net: a multimodal attention-enhanced segmentation network for detecting lunar lobate scarps
ns1:item.dc:title: MALS-Net: a multimodal attention-enhanced segmentation network for detecting lunar lobate scarps
ns1:item.dc:creator: Xijian Li Man Peng Kaichang Di Bin Xie Bin Liu Biao Wang Li Li Sheng Zhang Jianzhong Liu a State Key Laboratory of Remote Sensing and Digital Earth, Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, Chinab University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, Chinac College of Geomatics, Xi’an University of Science and Technology, Xi’an, Chinad College of Resources and Environment Engineering, Guizhou University, Guiyang, Chinae Institute of Geochemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Guiyang, ChinaXijian Li is a Ph.D. candidate at the State Key Laboratory of Remote Sensing and Digital Earth, Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences. He received his bachelor’s degree in Geographic Information Science from the School of Environment and Surveying, China University of Mining and Technology in 2024. His research interests include planetary remote sensing, feature detection, and mapping.Man Peng received the Ph.D. degree in cartography and geographical information systems from the Institute of Remote Sensing Applications, Chinese Academy of Sciences, in 2012. She is currently an Associate Professor with the Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences. Her research interests include planetary remote sensing and mapping.Kaichang Di received the Ph.D. degree in photogrammetry and remote sensing from Wuhan Technical University of Surveying and Mapping in 1999. He is currently a Professor with the Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences, where he is the Founding Director of the Planetary Mapping and Remote Sensing Laboratory. His research interests include planetary photogrammetry and remote sensing, visual localization and navigation, and planetary science. Dr. Di was the Chair of Inter-Commission Working Group III/II “Planetary Remote Sensing and Mapping” of the International Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing from 2016 to 2022.Bin Xie is a Ph.D. candidate at the State Key Laboratory of Remote Sensing and Digital Earth, Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences. He received his bachelor degree in Surveying and Mapping Engineering from the School of Geosciences and Info-physics, Central South University in 2021. His research interests include planetary remote sensing image feature matching and high-precision mapping.Bin Liu received the Ph.D. degree in photogrammetry and remote sensing from Wuhan University in 2011. He is currently an Associate Professor with the Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences. His research interests include planetary photogrammetry and orbital data processing.Biao Wang is a Ph.D. candidate at the State Key Laboratory of Remote Sensing and Digital Earth, Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences. He received the B.E. degree in Space Science and Technology from Shandong University in 2022. His main research interests include planetary remote sensing geology and comparative planetology.Li Li received the Ph.D. degree in cartography and geographical information system from the Institute of Remote Sensing and Digital Earth, Chinese Academy of Sciences, in 2016. He is currently a college instructor in College of Geomatics, Xi’an University of Science and Technology. His research interests include remote sensing geology and planetary mapping.Sheng Zhang received the Master’s degree in resources and environmental engineering from the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences in 2023. He is currently working toward the Ph.D. degree in geology with Guizhou University. He is mainly involved in the field of planetary remote sensing and planetary geology.Jianzhong Liu received the Ph.D. degree in geoscience from Changchun College of Geology (now Jilin University) in 1996. From 1996 to 2000, he conducted Postdoctoral Research with the Institute of Geochemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences. He previously served as the Deputy Chief Designer of the Ground Application System for China’s First Lunar Exploration Project and the Deputy Commander of the Ground Application System for the Second Phase of the Lunar Exploration Program. He is currently a Professor and Doctoral Supervisor with the Institute of Geochemistry, CAS. He has authored or coauthored more than 200 research papers. His research interests include lunar and planetary geology, planetary remote sensing, and multimodal models for lunar and planetary science.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Cross-regional performance and generalization of deep learning models for fine-grained semantic segmentation of marine aquaculture cages
ns1:item.dc:title: Cross-regional performance and generalization of deep learning models for fine-grained semantic segmentation of marine aquaculture cages
ns1:item.dc:creator: Jialiang Liu Xiaomei Yang Zhihua Wang Yueming Liu Meiqi Zhou Jie Jiang a State Key Laboratory of Resources and Environmental Information System, Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, Chinab College of Resources and Environment, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, ChinaJialiang Liu received the B.S. degree from the School of Remote Sensing and Information Engineering, Wuhan University, in 2025, and is currently pursuing the M.S. degree in the State Key Lab. of Resource and Environmental Information System, Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS). His research interests include remote sensing, computer vision for Earth observation, and marine/coastal monitoring.Xiaomei Yang received the B.S. and M.S. degrees in photogrammetry and remote sensing from the PLA Information Engineering University in 1991 and 1995, respectively, and the Ph.D. degree in the Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, CAS, in 1999. She is currently a professor and Ph.D. supervisor at the Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, CAS, and the deputy director of the State Key Laboratory of Resources and Environmental Information System. Her major research interests include remote sensing image geoscience understanding and analysis, and geographic information systems in the marine and coastal zones. She has published more than 100 peer-reviewed papers and won the National Science and Technology Progress Award in 2005 in these areas.Zhihua Wang received the B.S. degree from the School of Remote Sensing and Information Engineering, Wuhan University, in 2010, and the Ph.D. degree from the Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, CAS, in 2018. He is currently an associate professor and master’s supervisor at the Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, CAS. He is also a member of the Youth Innovation Promotion Association CAS. He has published more than 40 peer-reviewed journal papers as the first/corresponding authors on topics of remote sensing intelligent interpretation and geoscience analysis, including the study of mapping the first global-scale spatial distribution dataset of aquaculture ponds.Yueming Liu received the B.S. degree from China University of Geosciences (Beijing) in 2014, the M.S. degree from the Aerospace Information Research Institute, CAS, in 2017, and the Ph.D. degree from the Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, CAS, in 2022. He is currently an Assistant Researcher at the Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, CAS. His major research interests include intelligent remote sensing interpretation, deep learning and spatiotemporal analysis of coastal zone resources and environments. He has published 10 peer-reviewed journal papers as the first/corresponding author.Meiqi Zhou received the B.S. degree from the School of Remote Sensing and Mapping Engineering, Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology, in 2024, and is currently pursuing the M.S. degree in the State Key Laboratory of Geographic Information Science and Technology, Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, CAS. Her research interests include remote sensing, fisheries geographic information science, and coastal zone scene classification.Jie Jiang received the B.S. degree from the College of Geography and Remote Sensing, Hehai University, in 2025, and is currently pursuing the Ph.D. degree in the State Key Lab. of Resources and Environmental Information System, Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, CAS. Her research interests include remote sensing, aquaculture facility extraction, and machine learning.
